Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Severe, persistent headache for 3 days; no clear trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Sudden onset on waking 3 days ago.
  - Continuous; partially relieved by ibuprofen but does not fully resolve.
  - Severity reported as 8/10, improving to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.
  - Not waking patient from sleep; present on waking.
  - Occasional stabbing pain when standing quickly; sensation of something “moving” when throwing head.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable):
  - Photophobia.
  - Visual disturbance described as “shooting lights.”
  - Denies sore throat, ear pain, sinus pain/pressure, cough, phlegm, nosebleeds, hemoptysis.
  - Denies changes in smell or taste.
  - No dyspnea, stridor/noisy breathing, throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling.
  - No neck pain or swelling reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - Prior intermittent headaches resolving within 2 days with ibuprofen; no prior similar prolonged/severe headache.
  - No prior hospital care or injections for headache.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: None reported.
  - Current meds: Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented). Oral contraceptive pill (name not documented), started ~1 year ago; no noted side effects. Acetaminophen use suggested in combination with NSAID (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context:
  - Lives alone; works from home. Has missed some work due to headache.
  - Tobacco: None. Alcohol: “three once a week” (units unclear).
  - No recent travel.
  - Family history: Mother has migraines with vomiting.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: Not reported.
- Airway/breathing: No dyspnea or noisy breathing reported.
- Mental status and associated features: Alert and coherent on call; denies focal neurologic symptoms (no tingling, numbness, weakness). Mild nausea, no vomiting.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (telehealth; no in-person exam performed).
- Presence of another person: Not stated (patient lives alone).

Assessment:
- Suspected migraine-type headache, possibly with visual aura (photophobia and “shooting lights”), first episode of this severity and duration.
- No reported fever, focal neurological deficits, or meningeal symptoms. Headache persistent for 3 days; partially NSAID-responsive.
- Consider contraceptive counseling if migraine with aura confirmed (combined oral contraceptive may be unsuitable).
- Justification: Acute onset, continuous course, photophobia, visual phenomena; partial response to NSAID; family history of migraine; absence of infectious or focal neurologic features per history.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Arrange in-person appointment via support team for full neurological examination and fundoscopic (optic disc) assessment; check blood pressure.
  - Prescribe a stronger NSAID alternative to ibuprofen (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); may take concurrently with acetaminophen; take with food.
- Specific instructions provided:
  - If the headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes character before the appointment, go to A and E for examination. Patient may call the clinic for further advice.
  - If symptoms settle before the appointment, the appointment can be canceled.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Worsening or changing headache, unbearable pain; new neurologic symptoms; any concerning change—seek urgent evaluation (A and E) as advised.
- Follow-up:
  - In-person evaluation with neurological and fundoscopic exam and blood pressure check.
  - Review suitability of current oral contraceptive if migraine with aura is diagnosed; may require change in contraception.
  - No COVID-19 vaccine discussion noted.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (BP, HR, temperature), full neurological exam, and fundoscopy not recorded.
  - Names and doses/routes/frequencies for: current ibuprofen regimen; newly prescribed NSAID; acetaminophen dosing.
  - Exact name/type of oral contraceptive; pregnancy status not discussed.
  - Detailed characterization of visual aura (duration, laterality), and comprehensive red flag screen (e.g., thunderclap onset, neck stiffness, jaw claudication) not fully documented.
  - Formal allergy list confirmation beyond “none reported.”
- Internal conflicts:
  - Alcohol intake documented as “three once a week” (units unclear/ambiguous).
- Transcript quality:
  - Several inaudible/omitted words and incomplete medication names; otherwise understandable.
